  • 1 for Guise, Captain Cosmic, and Visionary (3)

Here are some answers!

1) Someone asked a while back if the unlocked mini-expansions, and promos, and Void Guard expansion, are really free to all backers. The answer is yes, they are really free to all backers.

2) Someone correctly stated this, but I wanted to officially say it here: the Completionist Guise variant will appear in the following products: Ultimate Collector's Case, Complete Hero Variant Collection, and 5th Anniversary Foil Hero Collection. It will not be available outside of those products, so if you are not getting one of those products, you will not get it.

3) Every card in the 5th Anniversary Foil Hero Collection and the Complete Hero Variant Collection will have a different piece of character art on it than any other instance of that card in any other product that is currently available, or that will be available at the time of its release. This means that Adam is going to draw two pieces of character art for each of the new hero variants; one for the regular release, and another for those products.

So, this seems like a good place to post a list of everything I can confirm us getting, because it is making my head explode.

 

Base 5 heroes: Luminary, Harpy, Akash'Thriya, La Commadora, and Lifeline (previously Baron Blade, The Matriarch, Akash'Bhuta, La Capitan, and Deadline respectively)

6 stretch goal heroes: Stuntman, Benchmark, and the 4 Void Guard (Previously known as Ambuscade, {Revenant?} Writhe, Mainstay, Idealist and Dr. Medico respectively)

18 new variants: Omnitron-U, Parse (Fugue State), Extremist Sky-scraper, Visionary Unleashed, Captain Cosmic (Vengeance? Whispers of OblivAeon?), Completionist Guise, Luminary (Genderbent? Hero of the People?), Darkwatch Harpy, Stuntman (Ramboscade), Supply and Demand Benchmark, Akash'Thriya Spirit of the Void, La Comodora Curse of the Black Spot, Lifeline Bloodmage, the Five 90's Xtreme Prime Wardens (Argent Adept, Fanatic, Captain Cosmic, Haka, and Tempest)

There are an Unknown number of Environments in the Base, but we do know that Fort Adamant and The Nexus of the Void have been added, so 2 there and I'll assume at least 1 environement in the base.

"Several Villain Decks" according to the page in the Base. 2 Will be OblivAeon and the Aeon Men. Scions will make up the rest. I feel a minimum of 3 Scions, but if we use Progeny's deck as a reference we'll end up with 4 Scions (Flame, Blight, Storm and Frost)

 

So... staring at a minimum of 19 new decks with 18 variant cards coming down the pipe. And likely more than that. If we assume 3 environments base and 4 scion decks... 22 new decks of Sentinels goodness.

 

Oh and this is ignoring the Mission Deck since we have no idea how it will even work or effect the game.

#483

On saving money by buying during the Kickstarter: Yes, you'll save money ON THE RETAIL PRICE. Often, though, products are sold at a discount from wholesalers. Combine that with the ability to possibly save on shipping by getting many products from the same wholesaler, and it is far from guaranteed that the Kickstarter is the best way to get the very best price.

 

There are some things in this Kickstarter that you will have difficulty getting other places:

  • The new promo cards: Yes, you'd be able to later order the Hero Variant Collection, and thus get all of the cards, BUT the art on the new promos available via this Kickstarter is going to be different than the art in the Hero Variant Collection. So if you care about that and are not planning on being at a convention where GtG has a booth, this may be the only way to get _those_ cards with _that_ art save from buying them on eBay. Once you go the eBay route, you'd probably be saving money via the Kickstarter
  • The Canvas print: Apologies if I've missed it, but it's not clear that the canvas print will be available after the Kickstarter. My guess is that if lots of people want to buy this in the future that GtG would do create more, but I think it's more likely that they'll get enough to fulfill Kickstarter orders and maybe a bit more, and then this will become unavailable.
  • The Ultimate Collector's Box: They'll probably keep this in stock in their own web store, but it may be something that retailers aren't interested in and therefore distributors and wholesalers don't end up carrying it, so even if it _is_ available, it probably won't be available at a discount.

 

If your main interest is to get all of the cards and you don't care about having every single piece of art, and you don't need an extra box or a canvas print, AND YOU DON'T MIND possibly getting your games/cards later than other people, then you may have no particular need to order via the Kickstarter and can likely get a better price later.

 

Now, most of us may want you to order via the Kickstarter to help us get the total up to the unrevealed stretch goals, but don't kid yourself that you're saving money.

Powerhound_2000:

Just for reference I asked Christopher his expectations funding wise for OblivAeon and this was his response:

I had a good feeling that we would fund. Maybe even in the first week. I had a reasonable hope that we would break $100k, and thought that maybe, JUST MAYBE, we might break $200k. But that seemed highly unlikely.

This comes up time and again: Kickstarters like this one, or MST3K, or anything made by an established miniatures company, which seem totally assured to reach some absurdly high result.  I mean, I (obviously) don't have access to >G's financial information, but given the scope of the project, I'd have bet on this Kickstarter doing at least twice as well as Shattered Timelines, and probably closer to three times as well.  Now, obviously, that $360-545K estimate also fell far short of reality, but it's closer to the current total than to Christopher's guesses.

 

It seems like there's this strong trend among KS creators to be very conservative in their estimates.  I don't know whether this out of fear of somehow "jynxing" the results, or just humility, or what - I would have expected more overly-ambitious guesses if anything, but that's overwhelmingly not what I see.

 

I don't really have a conclusion to this - it's just some thoughts I was musing on.  In any case, a big congratulations to the whole >G team!  Try not to get buried in the avalanche of success (and work) descending upon you.

I think the reason for concern on reacing the $1M stretch goal is actually well placed. While I am confident we will make it, this campaign is very different from others that have this kind of start, and from many campaigns on KS in general.

The fanbase is already there, and most of those that have the game that want to expand have likely already hopped on KS and either pledged or intend to be reminded at the end of the run, the great majority being the former.

Other projects that make 1/2 their final pledge over the first 3 and last 2 days tend to have multiple add-ons (Arcadia Quest has so many...). Additionally, they are either entry level games, or you can get the core game in one of the pledge levels without a huge hit to your wallet. Here we only have The Entire Multiverse, which is a great thing to have, but not everyone can spend $400, so they will probably buy the core elsewhere and, if they like it, pick this up after the KS (unless they try the core soon!)

I fully believe that we can make the 1M, especially if we hit 750k by Monday, but I don't anticipate it soaring much higher than that. I think 1.25M would be pushing it at this rate, but I certainly hope they make as much as 2M for this glorious game :)

- Art print Set (the 8.5" x 11")

- Canvas Art (18' x 24"). Apparently this is unique to KICKSTARTER. "All canvas prints will be signed by Adam Rebottaro and are only available at the upper Pledge Levels."

Chaosmancer:

So, this seems like a good place to post a list of everything I can confirm us getting, because it is making my head explode. 

Base 5 heroes: Luminary, Harpy, Akash'Thriya, La Commadora, and Lifeline (previously Baron Blade, The Matriarch, Akash'Bhuta, La Capitan, and Deadline respectively)

6 stretch goal heroes: Stuntman, Benchmark, and the 4 Void Guard (Previously known as Ambuscade, {Revenant?} Writhe, Mainstay, Idealist and Dr. Medico respectively)

18 new variants: Omnitron-U, Parse (Fugue State), Extremist Sky-scraper, Visionary Unleashed, Captain Cosmic (Vengeance? Whispers of OblivAeon?), Completionist Guise, Luminary (Genderbent? Hero of the People?), Darkwatch Harpy, Stuntman (Ramboscade), Supply and Demand Benchmark, Akash'Thriya Spirit of the Void, La Comodora Curse of the Black Spot, Lifeline Bloodmage, the Five 90's Xtreme Prime Wardens (Argent Adept, Fanatic, Captain Cosmic, Haka, and Tempest)

There are an Unknown number of Environments in the Base, but we do know that Fort Adamant and The Nexus of the Void have been added, so 2 there and I'll assume at least 1 environement in the base.

"Several Villain Decks" according to the page in the Base. 2 Will be OblivAeon and the Aeon Men. Scions will make up the rest. I feel a minimum of 3 Scions, but if we use Progeny's deck as a reference we'll end up with 4 Scions (Flame, Blight, Storm and Frost) 

So… staring at a minimum of 19 new decks with 18 variant cards coming down the pipe. And likely more than that. If we assume 3 environments base and 4 scion decks… 22 new decks of Sentinels goodness. Oh and this is ignoring the Mission Deck since we have no idea how it will even work or effect the game.

Posted this a while back, felt like it was time to update it.

 

Still 5 base heroes (Luminary, Harpy, Akash'Thriya, La Commadora, and Lifeline)

Still sitting at 6 stretch goal heroes (Stuntman, Benchmark, and the 4 Void Guard)

We've got 22 new variants, but also I'm going to try and math out all the variants coming with the complete variant pack and the foil pack.

The KS campaign says 61 variants were coming with the Complete Variant pack, but that might be an updated number…yep, using the Wiki that seems to be an updated number. So I'll also use the 104 for the foil cards.

We've gotten confirmation of no additional environment decks, so we just have the 2.

No new information on the mission deck or vilain decks, so I'll stick with my minimum estimate of 5 all together (assuming Aeon Men deck is using the Scion Aeon Master as it's main villain.)

 

So, a total of (5+6+2+5) 18 decks of cards with (61 normal variants+104 foil cards) 165 new hero cards. Along with the comic and box and whatever else I forgot. This is getting pretty hefty.

skoticus:

 

MightySi wrote:
At the risk of being in a minority, by the sounds of it, I also don't ever use Parse as I'v never had her do anything useful in my games and she seems remarkably lackluster.I dont know what I am missing, but she jut stays in the box with Argent Adept and Nightmist as heroes that do nothing for me, fun-wise.  
I LOVE AA, and NightMist is my wife's favorite--both are awesome if you can get stuff going. But I'll also admit that though I like the idea of Parse, I've yet to find her useful.  I still try her out sometimes, because I have faith, but I am still waiting to figure out when she shines.

Scouting and manipulating the villain deck does enough 'damage' to the villain, IMO. Against certain villains, it prevents their best stuff from coming out (No Forced Deployments, Dark Heros, Galvanized, or any card that reveals the top H cards of the deck and puts these types of cards into play). Against others, it completely kills their turn (Hey Citizen Dawn, we'll let you play Citizen Spring, no problem! Omnitron, you can totally play that component that gives us an entire round to deal with instead of those blasted flechettes).

Irreucible damage in the right spot can totally turn the tide of the battle as well. Against Apostate, it means you can take out relics of your choosing, like that one that gives all other relics 2DR. Advanced Miss Information with her 2DR is usually annoying, but sometimes one turn of everyone doing irreducible damage to her is all you need to take her out.

She is also one of the few heroes that can destroy ongoings and environments as a power (Omnitron-X and Argent Adept being two other heroes that come to mind). That can save the heroes' collective bacon as well. 

If you want to deal large amounts of damage, then Parse isn't for you. The effect she has on the field isn't readily apparent, but in the right hands, the heroes will have a much easier time fighting the villain with her around.

I can remember once shooting something for about 23 damage after I'd saved up Critical Multiplier stacks for a while and had deliberately done anything other than attack stuff till I could let loose the big hit. I find that's ap retty satisfying thing on Parse - get out all three copies of Critical Multiplier, then play Recompile as often as you can get it and just dump all the Critical Multiplier stacks on someone who can do other things besides hit something every turn, so they can one-shot the last half of the villain's hp away after a few turns or something :D.

The Adept can be effective with just two or three cards out, depending on which ones they are and on the current gameplay situation (ie what kind of abilitis would be useful right now). I had one game against awn where due to constantly having tuff broken I never got out more than two songs and an instrument at any one time, I don't think, yet we managed just fine and I think we won in the end as I kept giving people extra card plays and stuff. Alacritous Subdominant alone, for example, would make Unity very happy and you don't even need any instruments (assuming you're playing the base version of the Adept) :D. In other news, finding out somehere earlier in this thread (I think) a few days ago that the Adept is asexual I thought was pretty cool too - I think I like him even more now :D.

For those who prefer not to play certain characters because they can't really get a grasp on how to play them effectively (or can't really see what kind of use their deck can have), have you ever played in games with other people who do play those characters? It may help you see other ways of playing the character outside of the way you've been trying to play them and you may realise new tricks or methods to them that may make them more enjoyable. Off the top of my head, I think Fanatic and Setback are two that I'm not really a fan of playing too much. #707
skoticus:

But I'll also admit that though I like the idea of Parse, I've yet to find her useful.  I still try her out sometimes, because I have faith, but I am still waiting to figure out when she shines.

Try and play her against the Chairman. When you remove every Prison Break from the equasion using Buffer Overlow/Extrasensory Awarness/Updated Intel, make short work of all the villain targets played due to the extra damage from Exploit Vulnerability, and allow your teamates to do crazy things with Syntactic Analysis/Critical Multiplier/Between the Lines, you will learn how truely terrifying her deck is. If she can GUT the Chairman, she can do the same thing to just about any other villain deck.

You have to play Parse with the same mindset you would play Visionary. She is a deck manipulation master, and frankly is much better at it (Visionary brings things like Twist and Mind Control however and DVis has manipulation build in at the base, and while those are much more situational, they are strong in their own right). Maybe doing that or playing that way doesn't seem "glorious" and I can see that being the case. But if you want to talk about the best way to "Win" the game, dictating the entire villain deck to the extent that Parse can strongly flirts with the edge of gamebreakingly powerful.

People who demand pandering. One of the great things about Sentinels is that it DOESN'T pander. You have Unity who's Jewish- but it doesn't feel like she's there just to be the token Jew; she just happens to be Jewish, there's more than that to her character. Similarly, Tachyon is a lesbian- but she's no there to be the token lesbian; rather, she just happens to be lesbian, and there's more to her character than that. Then there's Parse; if I felt like Parse was there to sell me the game as someone with autism, I would have probably stopped buying the game; but I never get that feeling- she's a character that happens to be autistic, and she's not there just for the purpose of trying to sell me the game. Actually, I'd go so far as to say that if I didn't bother to seek out the profiles and learn more about the characters, I probably wouldn't even know any of these things about them. It's not about representation, it's about writing characters, and that's how it should be- because no character can truly represent real people, and to insinuate they can is insulting to anyone that they're attempting to represent.

From what I've seen, SJWs generally seem to feel like the best thing a character can be is as far removed from the average as possible- but this generally just results in characters that are such one-dimensional stereotypes that they're boring to read about. And the whole purpose of SJWs seems to be to try and create division and hatred between two groups most of the time, especially amongst those that generally would get along just fine.

Estelindis:

I thought Parse has Asperger's, but hey.

Asperger syndrome is autism. The DSM-5 replaced autism, pervasive developmental disorder-not otherwise specified, and Asperger syndrome with a single diagnosis - autism spectrum disorder. Diagnostically speaking, what someone would be diagnosed with depended more on where they were diagnosed than it did on which profile they fit. Plus, a lot of people diagnosed with AS met the criteria for autism.

Sorry if that was a bit lecturey, I have a tendency to infodump.

Thirdly, the point I was making was that we shouldn't need a character to be just like us to enjoy a game; honestly, if a game character was just like me, I wouldn't bother- I spend enough time being me in real life, I don't need that in a game. Fourthly, no one was complaining about diversity; once again, this makes me question if you even read the post I made beyond the first few words.
Silverleaf isn't being bigoted. The reason she brought up straight white dudes is that she made a comment about Parse not being a straight white dude earlier in the thread and you responded with a comment about SJW bigotry. You later produced a straw man about how so-called "SJWs" want pandering and not fully realized characters, which is 180 degrees from anything I've ever seen in the real world. If you want to complain about pandering, it'd help to have actual instances of a) pandering and b) people demanding pandering to talk about. Since neither is in evidence here, why are you so worried about it?

Thanks Belle. I tend to respond negatively to someone who uses a pejorative term (SJW) for anyone who would prefer representation and accuses people of "demanding pandering" when no one has done that.

It's very common to hear things like "You SJWs just want to ruin everything! If we include women and gays and blacks it'll make everything SUCK!". "SJW" is a term designed to belittle anyone expressing liberal or progressive views so you don't have to listen to them any more. Just like calling someone a "hater". I hear anyone using SJW in a serious way, I assume they are a Gamergate bottom-feeder, because it's a Gamergate buzzword.

Of course, it's very easy to say that you shouldn't need characters to represent you when 95%* of characters already do represent you. (And 4% are horrible stereotypes of marginalised groups, and/or sex objects.) I am extremely pleased that Sentinels doesn't follow the norm here.

 

  • I made that number up. It feels like that though, speaking as a person who is non-male, non-straight, and non-cis, it can be extremely difficult to find a character who I have anything in common with. And if you experience that enough, you start hearing "Games. Are. Not. For. You."

It's this type of thing that worried me, as it tends to be more divisive than anything, and feels like those that typically make such comments are the very thing they claim to be against…But I'll go ahead and stop here; this really isn't the place to be discussing this, it just struck a nerve is all. Sorry for any interuptions it may have caused.

"Abnormal" totally has negative connotations. I don't have any problems with acknowledging differences between people, and I wasn't in any way trying to say that people with autism (or any other group) are exactly the same as people without autism. I have a cognitive disability myself but I would hate for anyone to describe me as "abnormal".

My point was that many people with Asperger's don't consider themselves to have a disability and argue that the differences we see are just a spectrum of thought patterns and behaviours that don't need to be classified as normal/disordered because that variance itself is normal. It's not my place to label those people in a way they dislike, which is why I don't like to use "neurotypical" as it sets up non-disabled as the "ideal" and disabled as "other" or "non-ideal".

I apologise if I've upset you with that, but believe me that my intentions were to avoid upsetting people by using a term I know to be problematic.

I've been playing around with a spreadsheet to try to get a guessimate of how the KS will do, when it'll hit a million, etc. It looks at multi-day trends (and then multi-day trending of the trends) to predict the next day's pledge amount, and then uses the trend-of-the-trend to project further into the timeline. Like Kicktraq it's wildly inaccurate at the start, but I believe mine gets better at a faster pace than Kicktraq (which still thinks OblivAeon will hit 2.5 million, which would be great, but seriously???).

Anyway, early on in had 750K all the out at 3 March and little to no hope of 1 million. By yesterday, the magic day for 1 million was next week Tuesday, with a final total of 1.3 million.

Yesterday's total, though, was lower than projected.  Plugging in yesterday's total, the trends recalculated and pushed the 1 million day out to the 28th, with a final total at 1.06 million.

What this does NOT account for:
        Friday bumps as people get paid and set aside money before pledging
        weekend dips, though the multi-day trending levels that out (somewhat)
       the final 48 hour jump that many KS see

This is all just my ridiculously long-winded way of saying, I still think we'll get to 1 million, but I don't feel the need to check the KS total every 5 minutes.

As you were...

What we know so far:

2 zones, each with an Environment.

You skip your play, power or draw phase to move between zones.  If you "Hang out" in OblivAeon's zone he hits you for like 5000 irreducible damage.  Zone 1 contains a shield.

In Zone 2 you have the mission deck that rewards you for doing certain things, and gives you powerups to defeat the Scions and I assume use against OblivAeon.

 

Assumptions:

You have to bring down the shields, probably by finding furry creatures that will help you storm a bunker full of enemy troops.

You have to find something to stop the insta-Death OblivAeon attack, or maybe it goes away with the shield?  I assume you won't be winning the game by having Nightmist or Tachyon redirect the incredible damage back at OblivAeon for the win.

 

Christopher said it would take about 90 minutes (I assume for groups that know what they are doing).  So that means the missions can't be very time consuming to complete, and OblivAeon can't be too hard to take down once you are ready to fight him.

Really, meaning no offense to the Playtesters (envy, sure - it bugs me so much how the "adding extra testers" announcements seem to come exclusively when I'm not watching GTG so closely), I'd expect that the bigger issue is making sure that all the Heroes' base cards are set up correctly - variants are by nature optional, and I'm not even sure it's desireable for them to be carefully balanced against the main versions.  I find things like Freedom Six Tempest to be useful balance tools, and I don't think the likes of Team Leader Tachyon are less beloved due to being wildly out of scope with Tacyon's base power.  So long as a promo is interesting, the world doesn't end if it's wildly better or worse than the card it replaces.  People can just not use this optional widget that they spent essentially no money on.

 

Hero decks are a whole other story, of course, since they're such a huge part of the player experience, and other than swapping character cards there is no way to customize them.  Likewise, the base version of a character card will be seen by more people, and for many players may be the only version of the character they ever experience.  So I wish the testers all the luck in the world getting those character cards just right before the deadline*!  The rest... I simply wish for them to find interesting.

 

* Or is it the Lifeline?

When it comes to playtesting promos, we're trying to get to something that makes the deck feel different (like how Young Legacy plays differently to her father). It's about variety, and getting you to play in a new way with the same deck.

It's totally important that the promo isn't that different on the power scale than the original. I mean if you had a hero whose base power was Draw a Card and the variant was Draw a Card, Play a Card, there is literally no reason to play the original. There's no point just being "interesting" if you make one of the other variants (or the base) seem weak in comparison, and discourage people from using them.

Which character card to use needs to be an interesting choice, not a no-brainer.

My current theory on what is going on with Freedom Six Wraith.

With the announcement of Sentinel Tactics: Battle For Broken City, we saw 5 Spite clones. We also learned that with the damages done to Rook City thanks to Deadline and Progeny, there were some issues with The Chairman's under ground facility that resulted in many of the clones not surviving. We know Deadline went to Earth to cause mass destruction to try and lure away OblivAeon. However, Iron legacy seems to have done that in his timeline, resulting in Deadline not taking notice of the planet. It also seems as though there is one OblivAeon that exist, traveling where and when as he pleases. Sincet the main timeline is the one he is more interested in, the Iron Legacy's timeline planet may not have a Progeny. Due to Deadline and Progeny possibly not attacking in the Iron legacy Timeline, it is likely that a lot more of the Spite clones could have survived. Perhaps The Wraith or Iron legacy instead initiated the reasoning as to why The Chairman went into hiding in his underground facility. 

We have no confirmation as to whether or not Freedom Six Wraith's artwork takes place prior to or after the final conflict with Iron Legacy. Going with that it is actually after the battle, then perhaps this is after The Chairman has come back, bringing even more Spite clones with him than he does in the main timeline. One of the first things he decides to do is to take out The Wraith, as she has taken over for him while he was away.

#964

I just think that this is how Christopher tells stories. No offense to Christopher, but he is not a great novelist. If he was, he would write a book. Instead he is a game designer. He has all the elements of the plot and the overarching story he wants to tell, but his talent is not writing it all down giving the characters the dialog that delivers the intensity that they deserve. So, through Adam he paints snap shots of important moments that fit with the plot that he wants to advance. He then leaves it to our imagination to fill in the details. It is actually a classical way of telling a story taken to the extreme. When Homer wrote that Helen of Troy was the most beautiful woman in the world he did not then describe her. By leaving Helen a blank canvas we can all imagine our own version of idea beauty. Yours will be different than mine. I believe that the same kind of thing is happening here. Of the whole Kickstarter I am most worried about the comic because I think it will be hard for it to live up to what we hope it will be…

Maynes32:

 

Spiff wrote:
 Powerhound_2000 wrote:
That has been the case for the entire game why change now?   
Because the game is done!The fact that everyone here has their own theories about what's going on in that pit tells me that we don't actually have the real story.  I have to admit that if I'm expected to buy the RPG to get the story for the game I've been paying for for 5 years, I may just say forget it.Yes, I'm in a mood today.
I had a long rant about this. Instead I'm just going to agree ;)

 

Here is what I think about the whole "story" of Sentinels of the Multiverse.  Christopher has given us a world and he hasn't given us much detail because of the title of the game itself.  The multiverse is us and while we have comic numbers listed on each card and we have no idea where they really fit in terms of an official GTG storyline, if all we wanted was that story, I'm sure it will be given to us eventually.  I think its fun to think that maybe we encounter some heroes that we see in the early boxes later, but they foreshadow what is to come.

Take the Visionary for example, if we were to look at a chronological timeline of the comic history, in my opinion, she would show up closer to the Shattered Timelines part of the story instead of near the beginning of Sentinel Comics due to her whole time travel thing.  However, others could see her coming in sooner, but even though we don't know when she actually shows up, we still include her in our fights against Baron Blade, Voss, Omnitron, and Dawn.  It would kind of suck to just have a character sitting in a box for story purposes, especially if that character is one of your favorites.  Heck, AZ doesn't appear until FFA#5 (I think, don't have the cards in my had atm).  

For me personally, I've been trying to figure out where characters and things take place from the cards for a long time mainly for fan fiction purposes, but you know what, that's the fun of having this multiverse, it is what you create.  Look at Razor's Edge, it's an awesome story, and it got placed in the SotM:VG.  Does it need more context than what it gave? Maybe, but is it any less good? Nope. I continue to write from time to time and even hope to put it in the fan fiction section again (it's been a while).  Whether people read it or not, it's the story I want to tell and ultimately people can enjoy that or not. Even in comics today with everything rebooting, they are starting with characters and a blank canvas essentially.  Where those writers/creators go with those stories is up to them, just as much as this story is up to us.

On that note, I would love to see the GTG storyline timeline just so I can see what Christopher and Adam had intended from their perspective.

Yeah, over in the thread discussing it, FV + Ra certainly seemed like the most frequent guess, so it interests me that so many people are surprised by it now.

 

You know what surprises me?  Bunker's outfit.  Legacy, Tachyon, and AZ all have a similar look going on, with more blue and fewer neutral tones.  Wraith doesn't really join in on that, instead opting for an outfit close to her Rook City get-up with a larger mask (SPOILERS: the mask is too little too late, and her secret identity gets out in the near future) - but she does add the same vertical lines on her torso which Legacy is now sporting, presumably presaging the grey "side panels" in the Tactics uniforms.  And then... Bunker is in this bright red suit with a glowing Arc Reactor, looking sinister as anything.  Let's be real, here - that's the suit Blade wears on his flip side, right?  I like to imagine that when he came to join up as "Luminary," Tyler Vance was totally against letting him do anything, and then he broke out the suit with a giant (angrily glowing) red bow on it, and then Bunker was all in favor.  Ah, well - at least he's not wearing Akash'Bhuta this time.

So, I knew I wanted to update my posts about how much stuff we are getting (I like to figure it out and write it down anyways so why not share it) but I also wanted to wait for the 1 million stretch goal so we can get an idea of actual size here. So, from the top if you will.

 

OblivAeon base game comes with:

 

5 base hero decks which are Luminary, The Harpy, Akash'Thriya, La Commadora, and Lifeline.

2 villain cards for OblivAeon along with 5 different shield cards

10 different Scions

As well as an OblivAeon Deck, Aeon Men Deck, Scion Deck and Mission Deck.

 

As stretch goals:

We unlocked an additional 6 hero decks which are Stuntman, Benchmark, and the 4 Void Guard

 

We unlocked 2 new Environments: Fort Adamant and the Nexus of the Void

 

We unlocked a lot of promo heroes:

"Old Heroes"-> 17

Omnitrion-U, Parse: Fugue State, Extremist Sky-Scraper, Captain Cosmic (Whispers of OblivAeon?), Visionary Unleashed, Completionist Guise, X-Treme Prime Wardens (Argent Adept, Fanatic, Captain Cosmic, Haka, and Tempest), Freedom Five (Legacy, Bunker, The Wratih, Tachyon and Absolute Zero), and Ra: The Setting Sun

"New Heroes"-> 11

Luminary (Hero of the People?), Dark Watch The Harpy, Stuntman (Ramboscade?), Benchmark: Supply and Demand, Akash'Thriya: Spirit of the Void, La Comodora: Curse of the Black Spot, Lifeline: Bloodmage, The Void Guard: Dr. Medico: Malpractice, Mainstay: Road Warrior, Super Sentai Idealist, and Cosmic Inventor Writhe

 

For a total of 28 new variants.

 

Then there is the Hero Variant pack, which should include around 67 Hero Variant cards with brand new art and the Foil Hero Collection which should ahve around 110 foiled hero cards. We also now have 33 Villain Oversized Foil Cards.

 

And the awesome Collector's box.

 

Oh, and there is a comic as well.

 

So, looks like (5+2+4+6) 17 new decks of cards with (28 stretch goal+67 variant pack+110 foil) around 205 variant normal sized cards and the 33 oversized cards.

 

This is utterly ridiculous and I love it. Of course, feel free to correct any mistakes I might have made, I'm posting this rather late after all
